evidence.q1: Hero band fills the viewport: 'On the shelf, not in a warehouse.' plus a two-line subhead saying they have been on Mill Street since 1961 and will set your order behind the counter within the hour.
evidence.q2: Primary button 'See what's on the shelf' and a 'Pickup list (0)' button in the header are both above the fold, with 'How pickup works' beside the CTA.
evidence.q3: Featured section holds five items in a deliberately unequal grid (one large plus one, then a smaller row); the pickup steps are a numbered vertical sequence and the staff section lists four people, so no standalone triad.
evidence.q4: The space beside the headline is a live 'Will-call shelf' card listing three named customer orders with times and a reserve-by cutoff, not decoration.
evidence.q5: Featured tools ('On the shelf this week'), seasonal guides ('Project sheets' with Spring/Summer/Fall/Winter tabs) and pickup ('How pickup works') each get their own region in the brief's order.

evidence.q1: 'Seventy-four years on Elm Street. Now we're online, too.' with a four-line paragraph explaining same-shelf, same-price ordering occupies the whole first screen.
evidence.q2: 'Shop what's on the shelf' primary button, a 'Pickup order 0' button and an 'In-store pickup' nav link are all in the first viewport.
evidence.q3: The band under the hero carries four claims, featured tools run six items and the seasonal guides run one feature plus six more; the pickup steps are an ordered ONE/TWO/THREE sequence, not peer cards.
evidence.q4: The right half is a drawn storefront showing the sign, the OPEN door and a curbside-pickup sandwich board, so it carries the store's physical claim rather than sitting empty.
evidence.q5: Featured tools, seasonal project guides and in-store pickup appear as three distinct titled regions in the brief's order, followed by counter services and family history.

evidence.q1: 'The whole store, aisle by aisle.' with the line about every item being counted on the Two Rivers shelves owns the blue hero, which fills the viewport.
evidence.q2: A 'Reserve for pickup' button sits inside the hero product card, with 'Browse the front table' and a header 'Pickup list (0)' beside it.
evidence.q3: The front-table section is six items in a one-plus-two-plus-three arrangement, the pickup band is an ordered Step 1/2/3 process, and the three names at the bottom are the three generations the brief itself names.
evidence.q4: Beside the headline is a full product card with price, counter, bin, SKU, on-hand count and a reserve button.
evidence.q5: All three named regions are present and titled ('This week on the front table', 'In-store pickup, and only in-store pickup', 'Seasonal project guides'); pickup precedes the guides, which still reads as the natural next question after the products.

evidence.q1: 'Seventy-five years on Water Street. Now on the internet, too.' plus a paragraph about 14,000 items at aisle prices dominates the first screen.
evidence.q2: 'Shop featured tools' primary button, a 'Pickup store' selector and a cart with count are all above the fold.
evidence.q3: The project-guides section shows exactly three equal cards in one row (deck sealing, weatherstripping, snowblower) even though the brief never counts three, and the hero closes on a three-up statistic row (2 hours, $0, 30 days).
evidence.q4: The right half holds a storefront illustration attached to an address card reading '214 Water Street' and 'Two marked pickup stalls out back'.
evidence.q5: Featured tools, fall project guides and in-store pickup each occupy their own labelled region, in the brief's order, before history and counter services.

evidence.q1: 'See the shelf before you drive over.' with the paragraph about counting shelves every morning is the largest thing on the page and anchors the first screen.
evidence.q2: 'Browse today's shelf' sits in the hero and three 'Hold it' buttons plus a header 'Pickup list 0' are visible without scrolling.
evidence.q3: The hero's right half is a row of exactly three equal product cards (labelled '3 of 14 seasonal items'), a triad the brief never asked for, even though the main shelf grid below runs eight items.
evidence.q4: The space beside the headline is those product cards, carrying aisle, bin, stock count, price and a hold button.
evidence.q5: 'Today on the shelf', 'This month's project' with 'The rest of the guides', and 'How pickup works' are three separate regions in the brief's order.

evidence.q1: 'Check the shelf before you drive over.' with the live-counts-and-pay-at-the-counter paragraph fills the first screen as one region.
evidence.q2: 'Browse featured tools' is the hero's primary button and 'Your list (0)' sits in the header, both above the fold.
evidence.q3: Featured tools are one large card plus a five-row list, the September jobs are one expanded plus two collapsed rows, and pickup is an ordered Step 1/2/3; the only three-up element is a thin inline stat caption, not a peer card row.
evidence.q4: Beside the headline is a dark store card with today's hours, where the pickup counter is, orders waiting, average pull time and a signed note from the third-generation owner.
evidence.q5: 'On the floor this week', 'What to get done in September' and 'Your list for the counter' plus 'How pickup works' cover the three named sections in the brief's order.

evidence.q1: 'The part you need is already on the shelf.' plus the reserve-and-hold line and the store's history own the left column and set the first screen.
evidence.q2: The pickup ticket form itself is in the first viewport, ending in a 'Send to the counter' button, alongside 'See what is on the shelf'.
evidence.q3: Featured tools are a six-item grid, the guides are one feature plus three text rows, pickup is a numbered vertical sequence and the FAQ is four items; nothing presents a bare set of three peers.
evidence.q4: The space beside the headline is a working will-call ticket with name, phone, pickup-time select and submit button.
evidence.q5: 'On the shelf this week', 'Project guides' (marked Autumn, four guides) and 'How pickup works' are three separate regions in the brief's order, with an FAQ after.

evidence.q1: 'Order it here / Pick it up here' with the line about seventy-seven years on James Street and a first website dominates the dark hero, which fills the viewport.
evidence.q2: 'See what's on the shelf' is the hero's primary button and a 'Pickup list 0' button sits in the nav, both above the fold.
evidence.q3: The shelf section is six items in an unequal arrangement (one large, two stacked, three smaller), the guides use a tab set over one long procedure, and pickup is an ordered 1/2/3 sequence; no standalone trio of peers.
evidence.q4: Beside the headline is an OPEN panel with today's hours, same-day cutoff, orders waiting at the counter, paint-counter hours and directions to the counter.
evidence.q5: 'On the shelf this week', 'Projects for the next six weeks' and 'Pickup at the James Street counter' are three distinct regions in the brief's order, with counter services after.
